To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the use of the architectural template presented in this work allows a more efficient exploration of the design space for H.264 block matching motion estimation arrays, leading to the identification of a novel architecture able to process CIF sequences with 60fps, and with an equivalent gate count of 2, 5 and 3 times smaller than the ones reported in the recent literature for similar architectures.

the use of a flexible template for the allocation of PEs within H.264 block matching motion estimation arrays is a very powerful tool to explore the influence of the computational resources allocation in terms of final area, dynamic power and processing speed.

(1) The use of a highly flexible architectural template has enabled the exploration of different design alternatives of H.264/ AV C block matching motion estimation arrays; (2) A novel motion estimation architecture composed of four groups with four P Es each has been proposed; (3) This new architecture is able to process CIF @60fps sequences with reduced equivalent gate count, dynamic power dissipation, and processing time.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the study and exploration of different alternatives for the allocation of the computational resources, allowing the establishment of a new design tradeoff in the context of H.264/ AVC motion estimation architectures.
the exploration of different allocation alternatives of computational resources within H264/AVC Block Matching motion estimation architectures.
the design of efficient motion estimation architectures for H.264, with special attention to the allocation of the computational resources.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the use of a flexible template for H264/AVC motion estimation architectures is a very useful tool for evaluating different design tradeoffs and exploring the impact of the allocation of computational resources in the area, dynamic power dissipation and maximum processing speed of the resulting architectures.

the allocation of the computational resources is a fundamental issue in the design process of motion estimation architectures and the introduction of flexible architectures, such as the one presented in this paper, is a must in order to achieve the best possible performance in terms of area, power consumption and processing speed.

the proposed template is a powerful tool for exploring the different alternatives in terms of area, processing speed, dynamic power dissipation, and memory size of H.264/ACV block matching motion estimation arrays.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the presented architectural template is an efficient way to explore the design space of H.264/ AVC block matching architectures.
the proposed template is a flexible tool for the exploration of the design alternatives in terms of the area and power consumption of H.264/ AV C block matching motion estimation arrays.
the proposed template is an efficient tool for the exploration of different allocation alternatives in the design of motion estimation architectures.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a proper allocation of the computational resources is a critical factor in the design of H.264/ AVC motion estimation architectures.
the allocation of the computational resources in the motion estimation architectures is a relevant issue to be considered when designing high performance video encoding systems.

the proposed architectural template is able to provide an efficient and flexible design methodology, allowing a better understanding of the influence of the different design tradeoffs in the overall architecture performance.
